evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Counted by two. Signed by two. Written down once.' plus lede 'Tallyhall keeps the books for churches and small charities. Two volunteers count the Sunday offering on a phone...' and CTA 'Start your free 60-day trial' say what, who and next step in one screen. The H1 alone is a slogan; the lede does the explaining.
evidence.fit: Both audiences are served: treasurer via the demo and 'What it takes off the treasurer's desk', committee via a 'For the committee or trustees' Q&A plus a 'Print a summary for the committee' button (print-only summary in DOM). Not-a-processor constraint stated under the hero and in its own section. Tone is warm, not corporate. But the structure (replaces table, four numbered steps, dark feature band, icon list, FAQ grid, CTA card) is a familiar SaaS sequence that hedges rather than resolves.
evidence.distinctiveness: Ruled-ledger lines behind the hero and the strike-through 'What you have now' column with the note 'Struck through with a single line, the way a ledger correction should be' are genuinely product-derived ideas. The rest is the standard kit: phone mockup in a dark bezel, 4-step numbered row, dark-green band with a tilted 'Sample' statement card, three icon rows, 2x3 FAQ grid, CTA box.
evidence.proof: A working phone-count demo sits in the first screen at 1440: I tapped + on £20 and − on £10, total moved £1,345.85 to £1,355.85; 'Finish count, ask both to sign' -> two signature cards -> 'Posted to the ledger' with a highlighted 19 Oct ledger row at £1,355.85. Numbers are consistent (statement 120+120+150+160 = £550). But it never shows why two counters matter (nothing can disagree), and the sample date 'Sunday 19 October' is a Monday in 2026 while the statement says 'Giving statement, 2026 / Total given in 2026' for a year not yet over.
evidence.craft: Clean type pairing (serif display + Inter-like UI), consistent green palette. Defects: at 1440 the left hero column is vertically centred against the phone, so operating the demo moves the H1 (top ~276px in Count state, ~210px in Sign state, ~240px in Posted) - the headline jumps when you click. Phone step labels '1 Count / 2 Sign off / 3 Posted' are 11.52px; axe reports 2 serious colour-contrast nodes at 390 and 1440. The 1440 hero has ~90px of empty ruled space above the headline while the phone runs below the fold.
evidence.mobile: 390: stacks cleanly, no overflow, CTAs 358x48. But it is the desktop composition stacked: the demo is a phone bezel drawn inside the phone, inset ~25px each side, and starts ~720px down (only the currency toggle peeks in the first screen). Stepper buttons measure 28x28, currency toggle 34px tall, header 'Start free trial' 35px. Section nav links are simply hidden (display none) with no menu, so 'Year end' and 'For the committee' are unreachable except by scrolling.
evidence.honesty: Nothing fabricated: 'About 40 congregations. We don't publish their names or their figures' and 'It isn't a payment processor' are straight from the brief. The demo's label 'A working sample of the counting screen. Names and amounts are made up.' sits under the phone, below the fold at 1440 and below a tall phone at 390, so it arrives late; the statement does carry a 'Sample' tag. Trial CTA goes to the brief's URL.
evidence.interaction: All controls worked at 1440 and 390 with no console errors: +/- steppers update line and total, currency toggle swaps to dollars/bills/checks ($1,690.65, statement $675.00), sign buttons animate a signature and stamp 'Signed at 12:09', focus moves to the second signer then to 'Count again', which resets. Thin edges: − clamps at 0 silently (20 taps on £20 left 0 with no message), no way to make the counts disagree, no error or empty state, and the hero layout shift on every pane change.
evidence.copy: Specific and humane: 'Before anyone goes home', 'Nobody types the figures in again on Monday night', 'Get January back', 'Taking this to a meeting? Print a one-page summary for the agenda papers.' Some repetition: hero lede, the replaces table and 'How a Sunday works' each restate count/sign/post/statement in near-identical words.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, CTA and the live phone demo all visible (demo caption is not). 390: headline, lede and both CTAs fill the screen; the artifact is not in view (only the Pounds/Dollars toggle at ~730px), so nothing on the phone's first screen backs the promise.

problems: 390: the demo is a phone-inside-a-phone that starts below the first screen, with 28px stepper targets and no mobile nav; desktop composition stacked rather than recomposed.
The demo shows a happy path only: counts can't disagree, so the core reason for two counters is never demonstrated, and there are no error or edge states.
Hero layout jumps when the demo changes panes at 1440; plus 11.5px step labels, 2 axe contrast failures and a sample dated 'Sunday 19 October' that is a Monday in 2026.

evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Counted by two. Written once.' followed by a bold 'Tallyhall is bookkeeping for churches and small charities.' and the count/sign/ledger/statement sentence; CTA 'Start a free 60-day trial' with note 'eight Sundays of counting to show your finance committee before anyone decides'. The Counters / Treasurer / Trustees definition list beneath states what each role gets.
evidence.fit: Every role gets a real path: counters operate the sample count; the treasurer sees it post; trustees get their own section 'Trustees see two names against every Sunday's total' with a sample ledger that the hero count actually posts into (after signing, 18 Oct row became Ann P. 11:52 / Dev M. 11:54, £1,386.40, Posted; month total £2,360.95 -> £3,747.35). UK/US handled by a 'Counting in UK £ / US $' switch that also changes fund name, donor name and cheque/check spelling across the page. Not-a-processor stated under the hero and as the first open FAQ. Tone reads like a parish ledger, not finance software.
evidence.distinctiveness: Structure is built around the product's objects: a counting sheet with Ann/Dev columns, a ledger, a giving statement, a numbered offering envelope drawing, and 'Instead of' sketches of the spreadsheet, hand-addressed envelopes and paper counting sheet. Schola (schoolbook serif) + Carlito type, sage paper ground and ink-blue actions feel like church paperwork. Section layout is still a conventional split-columns sequence and the small 'Instead of' sketches lean decorative.
evidence.proof: The first screen at 1440 opens on a sample count that already disagrees: '£5 notes don't agree: Ann counted 9, Dev counted 8' with a red row and 'Total £5.00 short'. That demonstrates the core control (two people must agree) before any scrolling. Numbers are internally consistent: 100+620+380+40+63.40+178 = £1,381.40 vs Ann's £1,386.40; statement 20+20+840+100+20 = £1,000 for '45 envelopes and 1 cheque'; ledger 1,212.75+1,148.20 = £2,360.95. Sample statement uses the completed year 2025, and 18 October 2026 is a Sunday.
evidence.craft: Deliberate scale: big schoolbook H1, Carlito body, numerals right-aligned in the table with a double rule above totals, ink-blue/red reserved for action and disagreement. Smallest text 14px, axe clean at 390 and 1440. Minor: at 1440 the 'Trustees' section leaves a ~300px empty area under the ledger card on the right while the left column runs on; the red error banner in the hero is the loudest element on the first screen and competes with the CTA; disabled 'Ann has signed' buttons after posting are pale.
evidence.mobile: 390: genuinely recomposed. Hamburger 'Menu' opens a full list plus a full-width trial button and closes when a link is tapped (scrolled to #ledger, menu hidden). The count table drops the Ann column and shows 'Ann 2' under each item, steppers are 44x44, and the status bar is sticky: tapping 'Ann signs' at the bottom of the sheet while lines disagree showed 'Ann can't sign yet: £5 notes don't agree' pinned at the top of the viewport. No overflow at 390 or 320. Cost: the full sheet is ~900px tall, so the sign buttons are a scroll below the first screen, and the header has no CTA without opening the menu.
evidence.honesty: 'Sample count, written for this page.' is the first line of the artifact, visible at 1440 and 390; the ledger and statement each carry 'Sample ... written for this page' at their top. 'Nothing here is sent anywhere; it runs on this page.' sits beside the reset. 'About 40 congregations. None of them is named here, and we don't publish figures about them.' Trial links all go to https://tallyhall.example/trial. The caution reads as confidence, not a list of lacks.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390, no console errors. Signing while lines disagree is refused with a named reason; fixing £5 with + gives 'Both counts agree: £1,386.40. Ann and Dev can both sign now.'; Ann signs -> 'Waiting for Dev'; changing £50 after Ann signed cleared her signature with 'The count changed after Ann signed, so the signature was cleared.'; both sign -> posted, inputs locked, focus to 'Start the count again', ledger updates. Edge inputs handled: empty -> 'No figure from Dev for £20 notes', letters stripped with 'Numbers only: anything else was taken out.', 9999 -> '999 is the most £20 notes one line takes on this sample.', below zero -> clamp with message. Reset and UK/US switch each explain what happened. FAQ details open/close.
evidence.copy: Written in the counters' world: 'Recount, correct Dev's line, then both can sign.', 'Waiting for two signatures', 'coins by the bag', 'Easter cheque', 'so nobody copies a year of envelopes out by hand', 'Count next Sunday's offering with Tallyhall.' Terms (count, sign, post, ledger, statement) stay consistent; every button says what it does ('Ann signs', 'Start the count again'). Reading level suits a retired volunteer.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: promise, audience, CTA with what the trial is for, three role lines and the live sample count with its disagreement all in one viewport. 390: headline, lede, CTA and the top of the sample count including the red 'don't agree' status are in view; the sign-off and reset are below, so the believable part is only half shown on the phone.

problems: 390: the counting sheet is ~900px tall, so signing and the posted result need a scroll past the first screen, and the header offers no trial button until the menu is opened.
The red disagreement banner is the loudest thing in the 1440 hero and pulls attention from the trial CTA; a cautious visitor's first impression is an error state.
Uneven rhythm in the mid-page splits: ~300px empty under the trustees ledger at 1440, and the small 'Instead of' sketches feel more decorative than the product objects around them.

reason: B's first screen operates the exact thing the brief sells - two people's counts must agree before anyone signs - and that one artifact then flows into the trustees' ledger and the UK/US statement, with labels at the top of each sample and feedback that stays in view on the phone. A has warmer moments (the struck-through ledger correction, the committee print summary) but its demo is a happy path in a phone bezel, it is pushed below the first screen and cramped on mobile, and the layout jumps as you use it. I'd change my mind only if the red error-first hero tested as alarming with careful volunteer treasurers.
